intent: A vast round crater of banded terraced cliffs cut by pale ramps, its one pale road spiralling from the rim across cracked ice to a tall spire of ice off the centre, read from above as a dark-and-pale bullseye whose ramps and isle change with every seed.
requests: A cheap visible cliff for long terrace risers: the tileset's bluff runs cost about 16,600 parts on a 10k-cell crater wall, so the wall is drawn as painted outcrop bands instead.

A way to thin the ground-mist emitter density on large maps: mist is about one emitter per 170 walkable cells, which held this 180x180 crater to roughly 6,000 walkable cells under the 40-emitter budget.
A vertical face for a frozen fall: a painted cell ground only colours the terrace tops, so the falls read as pale patches on the steps rather than a curtain of ice down the cliff.
